JUDGEMENT CALLS -- the five middle-rail crossings S2..S6 are the whole story on this sheet
  S2 (319,496), S3 (126,502), S4 (545,502), S5 (672,504), S6 (796,509): all read as JUNCTION.
  Evidence. (a) I dumped the raw pixels at all five with inkmap.py win=20. Every one is a plain X: a ~3px vertical stroke running dead straight through a ~2-3px horizontal stroke, no widening at the crossing (dot scores 1.4/1.4/1.4/2.1/1.6 against a ~2.4 threshold, so no solder blob) and no semicircular hop or sideways jog on either wire (hop scores 3.6/1.9/0.0/3.6/0.0 against a 6.0 threshold). (b) There is not one hop, jog or bridged arc anywhere on this sheet -- I checked the turn statistics for all 20 sites and the largest paired turn is 3.6 degrees. The drafter therefore has no 'not connected' notation in use at all, so a bare X cannot be meant as a pass-over. (c) Structural evidence, which I find decisive: the middle rail passes through the exact midpoint of all five columns, in every case precisely between that column's upper device and its lower device. That is a deliberately routed node row, not five accidental fly-overs. (d) The dataset ink prior in the brief: a plain crossing with no dot and no hop is usually a real junction.
  What the other reading would have implied: reading all five as crossings would split the grid into five isolated 2-terminal column-midpoint nodes (V-AC bottom + I-DC top; Zener#6 bottom + Diode#14 top; Diode#3 bottom + Zener#10 top; Zener#4 bottom + Diode#13 top; Diode#5 bottom + Diode#15 top) plus a middle rail reduced to GND#7 - 9uF - 4uH - 2kOhm - GND#17 in series. That is not electrically impossible, so rule 1 does not settle it; I decided on the ink prior plus the node-row geometry, and I am recording it here as the one real judgement call in this image.
  S0 (544,278) JUNCTION. deg=3 T: column 3 hangs from the top rail (a ~15px pen overshoot pokes above the rail). The rail is continuous through it. Any other reading strands Diode #3's top.
  S18 (681,751) JUNCTION. deg=3 T: column 4 lands on the bottom rail from above; the rail is continuous. Any other reading strands Diode #13's bottom.

MERGE (one, and it is not a faded-pencil case -- it is a box-occlusion case)
  ['0.1','6.0'] joins the 5uH inductor's right lead to the top of column 2. The column-2 wire leaves the top rail at (320,277), which falls inside the annotated bounding box of inductor #0 (box spans x 219..323, y 236..293), so deleting the component box severed the join and left the column as its own run (the tracer even reported it as unused inductor port p2 at (320,295) with wire_len 102, matching Zener #6's top lead run exactly). I verified the ink directly with inkmap.py at (322,282): the top rail occupies y=273..276 and the column's first pixels are at y=277, x=319..322 -- continuous ink, a clean T. Without this merge Zener #6's top would sit on a one-terminal net.

CLASSES: all 19 match. I checked the four diode/zener pairs at 7x zoom because the distinction matters: the three Zener Diodes (#4, #6, #10) all have the Z-bent cathode bar (hook up on the right, hook down on the left) with the triangle pointing up into it; the four plain Diodes (#3, #5, #13, #14, #15) have a straight cathode bar. #15 at (795,650) is the closest call -- it has a small hook on the LOWER line -- but that lower line is the triangle's base overshoot, not the cathode bar, and its cathode bar at y~612 is straight, so plain Diode is right. #7 is a GND drawn rotated 90 degrees (bars vertical, lead exiting right) and #17 is a normal GND; both are correctly classed. Nothing to reclassify.
